recipes.title: Nasi Goreng (Indonesian Fried Rice)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of Indonesian nasi goreng fried rice topped with a fried egg, prawn crackers, cucumber and tomato garnish
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Wok-Frying at a Street Cart
recipes.prep_alt: A street vendor in Jakarta wok-frying nasi goreng at a traveling food cart at night

sections.heading: Steps
items: If using freshly cooked rice, spread it on a tray and chill uncovered at least 30 minutes — day-old, dried-out rice is what keeps the grains separate instead of turning mushy.
Dry-toast the terasi wrapped in foil over a low flame 30 seconds per side until fragrant, then crumble (or skip this if using a pre-toasted shrimp paste).
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 3–4 minutes until cooked through.
Push everything to one side of the wok, add the sambal oelek and terasi to the cleared space, and fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps with the back of the spatula, and toss to combine.
Pour the kecap manis and light soy sauce over the rice and stir-fry 3–4 minutes until every grain is coated a deep glossy brown.
In a separate small pan, fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Plate the fried rice topped with a fried egg, cucumber slices, tomato wedges, and crispy fried shallots.

recipes.title: Sate Ayam (Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce)
recipes.dish_alt: Skewers of grilled chicken satay with charred edges served on a banana leaf with red onion and salt
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Raw Skewers Before the Grill
recipes.prep_alt: Raw marinated chicken satay skewers laid out ready for grilling at a street stall

sections.heading: Peanut Sauce — Ingredients by Serving
rows: Red chilies (bird’s eye, or to taste)
Tamarind pulp (mixed with a little water)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Combine the chicken with the kecap manis, oil, garlic, and coriander in a bowl. Mix well, cover, and marinate in the fridge at least 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the peanut sauce: pound or blend the peanuts, candlenuts, shallot, garlic, and chilies into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in a splash of oil over medium heat 3–4 minutes until fragrant and the oil starts to separate slightly.
Add the palm sugar, kecap manis, tamarind, salt, and water. Simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thickened to a pourable, clingy sauce. Set aside.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers (soak bamboo skewers in water first if using).
Grill or broil the skewers 8–10 minutes, turning and basting with the leftover marinade, until charred in spots and cooked through with no pink at the center.
Warm the peanut sauce back through if it has thickened too much, thinning with a splash of water.
Serve the skewers hot with the peanut sauce spooned over or served alongside, with steamed rice or lontong and a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Gado-Gado (Vegetable Salad with Peanut Sauce)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of gado-gado with boiled potato, blanched vegetables, tofu, tempeh and hard-boiled egg draped in peanut sauce
recipes.prep_alt: A cook grinding peanut sauce paste in a large wok over a charcoal stove at a food stall

sections.heading: Peanut Sauce — Ingredients by Serving
rows: Tamarind pulp (mixed with a little water)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the peanut sauce: blend or pound the peanuts, garlic, chilies, and terasi into a paste.
Combine the paste with the palm sugar, tamarind, kecap manis, salt, and water in a small saucepan.
Simmer 5–6 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened and pourable. Set aside to cool slightly.
Blanch the long beans, bean sprouts, and cabbage separately in boiling water 1–2 minutes each until just tender-crisp, then drain and cool.
Arrange the boiled potato, blanched vegetables, cucumber, fried tofu, fried tempeh, and hard-boiled egg on a plate.
Spoon the peanut sauce generously over the top.
Scatter with crispy fried shallots and serve with krupuk crackers on the side.

recipes.title: Ayam Goreng (Indonesian Fried Chicken)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of Indonesian ayam goreng fried chicken leg served with lettuce, cucumber, tomato and sambal in banana-leaf cups
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Frying After the Spiced Simmer
recipes.prep_alt: Spiced chicken pieces frying in hot oil in a wok until deeply golden

sections.heading: Steps
items: Blend the shallots and garlic into a smooth paste (a splash of water helps), then stir in the coriander, turmeric, and salt.
Rub the spice paste all over the chicken pieces in a wide pot or deep skillet.

Add the galangal, bay leaf, lemongrass, and coconut water, and bring to a simmer — coconut water is the traditional braising liquid and gives the chicken its characteristic mellow sweetness; plain water works in a pinch.
Cover and simmer over low heat 20–25 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through and the liquid has mostly reduced.
Remove the chicken and let it sit uncovered 5–10 minutes to air-dry the surface — this is what lets it crisp up without any flour or batter.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep skillet to 175°C (350°F).
Fry the chicken in batches 5–7 minutes per side until deeply golden and crisp — the meat is already fully cooked, so you’re frying purely for color and crunch.
Drain on a wire rack or paper towels and serve hot with steamed rice, sliced cucumber, and sambal.

recipes.title: Mie Goreng (Indonesian Fried Noodles)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of glossy mie goreng fried noodles topped with fried shallots and chili, twirled onto a fork
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Tossing Noodles in the Wok
recipes.prep_alt: Noodles being tossed in a hot wok over an open flame at a street food stall

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Fresh yellow egg noodles (or dried, boiled)

sections.heading: Steps
items: If using dried noodles, boil until just tender, then drain and toss with a little oil so they don’t stick together.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic, shallots, and chili, stir-frying 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken (or shrimp) and stir-fry 2–3 minutes until nearly cooked through.
Push everything to one side, crack the egg into the cleared space, and scramble briefly before mixing it through.
Add the cabbage and carrot, stir-frying 1–2 minutes until just starting to soften.
Add the noodles, kecap manis, dark soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Toss everything together over high heat 2–3 minutes until the noodles are evenly coated and slightly charred at the edges.
Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Plate the noodles topped with crispy fried shallots, with a lime wedge on the side.

recipes.title: Beef Rendang
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of dark, deeply spiced beef rendang served beside woven ketupat rice cakes
recipes.prep_alt: Cooks in traditional dress stirring rendang in large woks over an open wood fire outdoors in West Sumatra

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef chuck or shin, cut into chunks
Dried red chilies, soaked (or chili paste to taste)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, and soaked dried chilies into a smooth spice paste, adding a splash of water if needed.
This is the week’s special dish — give it a little more stovetop time than the rest of the week, but there’s no need to babysit it all day; it’s a weeknight-feasible simmer, not an all-day project.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Fry the spice paste 5–7 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and darkened.
Add the lemongrass, turmeric, and kaffir lime leaves, frying 1 minute more.
Add the beef and stir to coat every piece in the paste, searing 3–4 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, tamarind, palm sugar, and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, 1½–2 hours, until the sauce has reduced and thickened and the beef is completely tender.
Stir in the kerisik (toasted coconut) in the last 20 minutes — this is what gives rendang its signature dry, deeply toasted finish.
Keep simmering, stirring more frequently as the sauce thickens, until the oil separates slightly and the sauce clings to the meat rather than pooling around it.
Discard the lemongrass stalk and lime leaves, taste and adjust the seasoning, and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Sayur Lodeh (Vegetable Coconut Curry)
recipes.dish_alt: A pan of sayur lodeh vegetable coconut curry with eggplant, long beans and tofu in a turmeric-yellow coconut broth
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Eggplant & Long Beans at Market
recipes.prep_alt: Fresh purple round eggplants, long beans and cucumbers piled together at a market stall

sections.heading: Steps
items: Blend the shallots, garlic, chilies, candlenuts, galangal, and coriander into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Fry the spice paste with the terasi and bay leaf 3–4 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer — don’t let it boil hard, or the coconut milk can split.
Add the eggplant and long beans, and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the tempeh and tomato, and simmer 5–8 minutes more until the vegetables are tender.
Season with the palm sugar and salt to taste.
Discard the bay leaf and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Pisang Goreng (Fried Banana Fritters)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden fried banana fritters served on a plate, crisp battered slices ready to eat
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Frying Bananas at a Market Stall
recipes.prep_alt: A vendor frying battered bananas in a wok of hot oil at a market food stall

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Ripe saba banana or plantain, halved lengthwise
Honey or sweetened condensed milk (to finish, optional)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Whisk the all-purpose flour, rice flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl.
Gradually whisk in the water until you have a smooth, medium-thick batter, similar to pancake batter.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep skillet to 175°C (350°F).
Dip each piece of banana into the batter, coating it fully.
Carefully lower the battered bananas into the hot oil, frying in batches so the pan isn’t crowded.
Fry 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown and crisp all over.
Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
Drizzle with honey or condensed milk while still warm, and serve immediately.
